messages:
alex: seeing a weird IOPS spike on ephem NVMe in ap-southeast1, GPUs failing to attach. provisioning queue stalling around 30-40s per attach.

oncall-bot: incident created #INC-2026-3223 - Ephemeral NVMe IOPS spike (ap-southeast1) — pager duty notified.
mira: can you paste iostat / ioping? suspect small random writes from janitor/scrub overlap.
alex: quick logs: `iostat -x 1 3` shows sda avg await 25ms, %util 95, r/s 1200 w/s 4800. ioping latency spikes to 40-60ms. nvme-cli smart log shows rising media errors on a subset but not fatal.
jordan: interesting — timeline shows a control-plane config push ~3h before the spike that added a proxy hop for the ephemeral-cleaner traffic (mesh-proxy v2). could be adding latency and causing fsync retries -> write amplification.
sam: that matches: we saw retries in kernel logs: `fsync: retrying write due to -EIO` and overlayfs metadata churn.
devin: can we confirm which service is hammering? `iotop -oPa` on a repro host shows `ephemeral-cleaner` PID with 2500 rows/s small 4K writes during the spike.
alex: yep, `du -sh /scratch` looks normal, but cleaner is doing per-file metadata updates rather than batching.
mira: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle the janitor to 1MB/s per worker, 2) disable mesh-proxy for cleaner path (roll back), 3) bump io_uring qdepth for attach path, 4) route provisioning fallback to dedicated capacity.
jordan: disabling mesh-proxy for cleaner seems low-risk and would prove hypothesis. can we flip a feature flag?
sam: canaryed the flag in eu-west1 earlier — it cut small-write IOPS by ~70% in that test.
oncall-bot: action item created: AC-3223-1 throttle-janitor, AC-3223-2 rollback-proxy-cleaner, AC-3223-3 increase-qdepth, assigned to @mira and @devin. ETA 30m.
devin: rolling rollback on proxy config to remove cleaner from mesh path for ap-southeast1 now. command: `kubectl set env deploy/mesh-proxy CLEANER_USE_MESH=false -n infra` (doing a staged rollout).
alex: after 5m: IOPS dropped ~60%, attach latencies fell to 6-8s, GPU provisioning resumed. attaching logs: `grep attach /var/log/provisioner.log | tail -n 20` shows retries cleared.
mira: good, but observed a few drives with elevated wear counters — need followup. long-term fixes: rework cleaner to do metadata coalescing + batched fsyncs, add client-side caching for cleaner ops, and add kernel-level IO cgroup caps for janitor.
jordan: also file to vendor: ask NVMe vendor to correlate SMART spikes with firmware patch; opening NVME-REQ-22 with their support.
sam: cost note: throttling janitor increases scratch retention by ~12% which may raise storage reprovision costs; quantifying impact for finance.
devin: next steps: (1) keep mesh rollback for cleaner until cleaner is patched; (2) ship janitor throttle in config; (3) schedule a canary of new cleaner that batches fsyncs next week; (4) create an alert for small-write iops per host > 2000 r+w/s for 5m.
oncall-bot: update: incident INC-2026-3223 status -> mitigated.
alex: thanks all — filing a retro doc and a ticket to refactor cleaner. putting a short playbook in runbook/storage for this pattern (proxy-induced fsync amplification).
mira: adding runbook entries now. also tagging product to discuss dedicated capacity fallback SLA that kicked in briefly.
jordan: FYI, adding a metric to console: percent of attach failures attributable to disk iop pressure.
sam: ack :thumbsup:
devin: closing loop: turning mesh-proxy back on for other traffic, keeping cleaner out until patch. will post PR link when ready.
alex: PR received and review scheduled. good job everyone.
